q: What does the 'C' in the CIA triad stand for?
why: Confidentiality, Integrity, Availability: the three things security protects.

q: Which port does SSH use by default?
why: 21 is FTP, 80 is HTTP, 445 is SMB.

q: What does DNS do?
options: Translates domain names into IP addresses
why: It's the internet's phone book.

q: Which is the correct order of the TCP three-way handshake?
why: Client says SYN, server replies SYN-ACK, client confirms ACK.

q: Port 3389 open to the internet usually means what's exposed?
why: Exposed RDP is a favourite way in for ransomware gangs.

q: Which of these is a private (internal) IP address?
why: 10.x, 172.16–31.x and 192.168.x are reserved for private networks.

q: What's the difference between hashing and encryption?
options: Hashing is one-way; encryption can be reversed with a key
Encryption is one-way; hashing is reversible
why: That's why passwords are hashed, not encrypted.

q: What is a 'salt' in password storage?
options: Random data added to each password before hashing
why: Salts make identical passwords hash differently and defeat precomputed tables.

q: The padlock in your browser means…
options: The site is safe and trustworthy
Your connection to the site is encrypted
The site is run by a bank
why: Phishing sites have padlocks too. It only means the connection is encrypted.

q: Which Linux command shows running processes?
why: ps (or top) lists processes, often the first look on a suspicious box.

q: On Linux, where would you usually find authentication logs?
why: auth.log on Debian/Ubuntu, secure on Red Hat-style systems.

q: What does chmod 777 do to a file?
options: Gives everyone read, write and execute permission
why: 777 is almost always a bad idea, since anyone can modify it.

q: An email says your account will be closed in 24 hours unless you log in via its link. Which red flag is this?
why: Artificial deadlines push people to act before thinking.

q: What is 'vishing'?
why: Voice phishing. Fake IT support calls are a classic.

q: What is spear phishing?
options: Phishing aimed at a specific person using personal details
why: Tailored messages are far more convincing than mass spam.

q: Which MFA method is most resistant to phishing?
why: They're bound to the real site's domain, so a fake site can't use them.

q: An attacker sends dozens of MFA push prompts until the victim taps Approve. What's this called?
why: Number-matching prompts make this much harder.

q: What is a SIM swap attack?
options: Tricking a carrier into moving your number to the attacker's SIM
why: Then SMS codes go to the attacker. Another reason to avoid SMS MFA.

q: What does 'double extortion' ransomware mean?
options: Encrypting data and threatening to leak a stolen copy
why: It's why backups alone don't solve modern ransomware.

q: What's the most important property of a ransomware-proof backup?
options: It's offline or immutable, so attackers can't encrypt or delete it
why: Gangs specifically hunt for and destroy connected backups.

q: Which type of malware spreads on its own without user action?
why: WannaCry and NotPetya were worms.

q: What does a RAT give an attacker?
options: Remote control of the infected machine
why: Remote Access Trojan: keyboard, screen, files, webcam.

q: What does EPSS predict?
options: The probability a CVE is exploited in the next 30 days
why: CVSS is severity; EPSS is likelihood. Use both.

q: What is CISA's KEV catalogue?
options: A list of CVEs confirmed to be exploited in the wild
why: If it's on KEV, attackers are using it. Patch first.

q: A CVSS 3.1 vector contains AV:N/PR:N/UI:N. What does that mean?
options: Local access, admin needed, user must click
Reachable over the network, no login, no user interaction
why: That combination is the worst case for reachability: anyone, anywhere, automatically.

q: What's the real fix for SQL injection?
why: Parameters keep input as data so it can never become SQL code.

q: Which item is #1 on the OWASP Top 10 (2021)?
why: Broken access control moved to #1 in 2021 because it's so common.

q: Which cookie flag stops JavaScript from reading a session cookie?
why: HttpOnly limits the damage of XSS.

q: SSRF tricks which machine into making requests?
why: Server-Side Request Forgery. It reached AWS credentials in the Capital One breach.

q: In the cloud shared responsibility model, who is responsible for configuring access to your data?
why: The provider runs the platform; your settings are your job.

q: What does SIEM stand for?
why: Where the SOC collects and searches logs.

q: A 'false positive' alert is…
options: A real attack that was missed
An alert that fired on harmless activity
why: Tuning detections to reduce these is a big part of SOC work.

q: What is MITRE ATT&CK?
options: A knowledge base of real attacker tactics and techniques
why: Defenders use it to map detections against how attackers really behave.

q: What usually comes first when you find an infected machine?
options: Post about it on social media
why: Contain the spread and keep the clues.

q: Which is NOT a phase of incident response?
why: 'Hacking back' is illegal in most countries. Leave that to law enforcement.

q: What's a typosquatted package?
options: A package with spelling mistakes in its docs
A malicious package named like a popular one (reqeusts vs requests)
why: One typo in an install command can pull in malware.

q: What's an SBOM?
options: Software Bill of Materials: a list of components inside software
why: It answers 'are we affected?' quickly when the next Log4Shell lands.

q: What is prompt injection?
options: A faster way to type prompts
Hidden instructions in content that hijack an AI's behaviour
why: AI agents that read web pages or emails are especially exposed.

q: What made Mirai's botnet so large?
options: IoT devices still using default passwords
why: A short list of factory logins was enough.

q: Which of these is legal and ethical practice?
options: Hacking a site to 'test' it without permission
Solving challenges on TryHackMe or Hack The Box
Guessing a friend's password as a joke
why: Only test what you own or have written permission to test.
